topic: linkedin tests ai content reporting tool
headline: LinkedIn adds button to report AI-generated ‘slop’
summary: The professional network is rolling out a new feature allowing users to flag low-quality, AI-generated content in their feeds.
details: LinkedIn is introducing a "Seems like AI slop" button to combat the growing issue of inauthentic, computer-written posts. This move reflects a broader industry trend to address the influx of AI-generated content across platforms.

The new reporting tool will provide valuable data to help LinkedIn tune its AI models and better identify "slop" content. This complements existing automation defenses that block hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts daily.

The company is also implementing new classifiers to reduce the visibility of low-quality content in suggested recommendations. Users will also privately see flags in their dashboards when their content is perceived as inauthentic due to heavy AI use, encouraging improvement.

Notably, LinkedIn is replacing its "enhance your post" AI writing feature with a proofreading tool, shifting focus from altering voice to refining existing work. This aims to distinguish between AI-assisted refinement and outright "slop" content.

Further enhancements include expanded profile and page verification options and the ability to block comments from unwanted company pages, all part of LinkedIn's effort to maintain a platform for genuine human connection and expertise.
